targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands tool calls, conversation history and persistent agent memory.
targetAudience.readerProblem: Useful external tool output can enter a thread without the execution binding normally used to establish provenance, yet erasing it would also remove evidence and utility.

whyNow: A same-day merged Codex change classifies standalone FunctionCallOutput without call_id as possible external context, can mark memory polluted under policy, preserves transcript attribution and still allows a separate image consumer to use the artifact.

externalHook.description: One artifact can remain visible and useful while being denied authority to shape durable memory.

coreProposition: For digital employees, provenance evidence, immediate content utility and durable memory-reuse authority should be separate governance decisions: external-context material may remain visible and useful while memory reuse fails closed, and a pollution state is policy evidence rather than authenticated-source proof or end-to-end safety.

originalValue.description: Separates evidence retention, task-bounded use and durable behavioral reuse, then shows why each consumer needs its own authority decision instead of inheriting one global trust bit.

readerTakeaway: Retain attributable evidence, authorize reuse by purpose and consumer, audit state transitions, and never promote a memory-eligibility flag into source authentication or universal safety evidence.

supported: Merged Codex code classifies FunctionCallOutput without call_id as possible external context.
With the configured policy enabled, demonstrated injection and fork paths can durably mark thread memory polluted.
Transcript paths preserve named tool attribution while non-text bodies use a placeholder.
Recent-image selection can still use standalone or unpaired tool-output images.
unsupported: That every tool output is untrusted
That missing call_id authenticates an external principal
That every memory or context consumer enforces the polluted state
That the implementation provides end-to-end contamination resistance
uncertain: Which consumers must consult memory eligibility before reuse
What evidence can safely requalify externally supplied content

firstPartyRole.rationale: The article develops a general memory-governance pattern for digital employees and agent runtimes without relying on a first-party project.

decisionReason: The merged implementation provides a concrete multi-consumer boundary, while the Research Object contributes an original and transferable authority model with explicit limitations.
